missing-if-match-428: Answer a missing `If-Match` on PUT and DELETE with 428: declare `[FromHeader(Name = "If-Match"), Required] string? ifMatch` so the OpenAPI document lists it as required, but `[ApiController]` turns the missing header into an automatic 400, so remove the `If-Match` entry from `ModelState` in an `IActionFilter` with `Order = int.MinValue` and throw the 428 from the service after the body checks; an invalid body or id mismatch stays 400, and keep `[ApiController]` on every controller so its operations stay in the document.
status-contract-documented: Annotate every action with `[ProducesResponseType]` for each status it can return, including statuses raised by filters and services (201, 200, 204, 304 and `ProblemDetails` with content type `application/problem+json` for 400, 404, 409, 410, 412 and 428), so the generated OpenAPI document declares exactly what the API answers.
etag-on-reads: Set the quoted `ETag` response header on every create, read and update response, computed with `SHA256` and never `MD5` or a counter, and make GET honor `If-None-Match`: a matching value answers 304 with no body.
cancellation-token-passed: Take a `CancellationToken` parameter in every controller action and pass it through the services to every EF Core call (`SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken)`, `SingleOrDefaultAsync(cancellationToken)`), never `CancellationToken.None`.
contract-without-entities: Return response types such as records from controllers, never EF entities, and keep counters, analytics, timestamps and other server-owned or derived values out of every request and response schema.
request-bodies-required: Declare the request bodies of POST and PUT as required with a non-nullable body parameter, never `[FromBody] T?` or `EmptyBodyBehavior.Allow`, so the OpenAPI document marks the body as required.
